goal: Use Obsidian as the human governance layer for DC-Agent memory, with audited sync-back and approved-only runtime recall.

acceptance_criteria.description: Memory candidates export from data/nas_memory.db to Obsidian governance notes with stable memory_id, source_path, source_hash, review_status, sensitivity, and governance_version frontmatter.

Edited Obsidian governance notes import back into data/governed_memory.db idempotently: an unchanged note for the same memory_id creates neither a duplicate governed memory nor duplicate import audit.
Approved governed memories are promotable; rejected, merged, stale, and sensitive_blocked memories are not promoted to runtime recall by default.
Every state-changing Obsidian import decision and runtime promotion writes an append-only audit record with actor, action, memory_id, payload, and timestamp.
Runtime recall defaults to approved-only governed memories and excludes need_review, rejected, merged, stale, secret, and sensitive_blocked records unless an explicit admin path asks for them.

The production system preserves current NAS memory, Obsidian RawRefs, chat review capture, and dc_router memory_injection recall paths as reusable inputs instead of replacing them with an incompatible memory stack.
The first production version explicitly excludes an Obsidian native plugin, realtime Obsidian file watcher, bulk proactive review pings, and automatic deletion/forgetting from required scope.
Periodic promotion reconciles approved memories into runtime outputs idempotently: an already-current projection is reported as unchanged and creates no duplicate promoted_to_recall audit.
The governed-memory importer consumes only notes carrying its memory_id schema and ignores EmployeeInsight or other governance schemas without failing their independent approval workflows.
Company-fact recall combines approved governed memories with relevant NAS project and document evidence instead of letting one approved match hide supporting or conflicting source material.

Company-fact recall resolves matching Obsidian entity, department, and person bridge pages into bounded deduplicated relationship context while treating generated bridges as indexes rather than approved facts.

The Obsidian generator creates review-required canonical company, management, core-department, and client context pages from configured facts, links them from a company cognition index, and leaves priorities, preferences, current status, and decision criteria for explicit human confirmation.

non_goals: Do not replace data/nas_memory.db as the raw source memory index.
Do not require a native Obsidian plugin for the first production version.
Do not require realtime file watching for Obsidian edits in the first production version.
Do not use data/router_review_candidates as a production review queue.
Do not promote unreviewed or sensitive-blocked memory into default runtime recall.
Do not implement automatic deletion or forgetting before a retention policy exists.
Do not require full AstrBot KB write-back for assistants that can query governed NAS memory directly.
Do not add bulk proactive review pings as part of the first production version.

production_recall: optional AstrBot KB mirror for compatibility
